biography.plain_text: Mikhail Lesin was a Russian media executive and co-founder of Video International, a leading television advertising agency. He served as press minister from 1999 to 2004 and later as a presidential adviser. His career crossed commercial media and government, culminating in the leadership of Gazprom-Media. He died in Washington in 2015.

long_biography.plain_text:
Before entering television, Mikhail Lesin trained as a civil engineer and worked on construction projects in Moscow and Ulaanbaatar. Commercial entertainment offered a different direction: he helped organise concerts, ran a cooperative producing KVN comedy programmes and directed the television programme Vesyolye Rebyata. That grounding in production preceded his influence over the institutions financing and distributing Russian television.

As press minister, Lesin became directly involved in the struggle over Media Most, the owner of NTV. In 2000, he endorsed an agreement linking the termination of criminal proceedings against its owner, Vladimir Gusinsky, to a sale to Gazprom. The European Court of Human Rights ruled in 2004 that the detention had been used for an improper purpose in commercial negotiations, finding Russia in breach of the Convention.

uncertainties: All terminal private-wealth judgments use November 2015 as the time basis. Current corporate websites and later ownership changes are not attributed to the deceased person.

The original advertising business provides positive private-wealth evidence. His government posts, influence over media regulation and Gazprom-Media executive role do not establish ownership of state or corporate assets. The primary industry is an explicit origin-sector fallback.

Forbes 2014 was directly read. It records his denial of owning a business and denial that the disputed US family properties were his; no property value or family assets are counted as his wealth. Broad self-made is an inference about the documented original business mechanism, not a statement about the legality or full provenance of all assets.

The court judgment is a human-rights ruling against Russia. Its undisputed agreement and detention findings support the central controversy; they are not a criminal conviction of Lesin. No claims of murder, money laundering or other unadjudicated wrongdoing appear in published prose.
DOJ closed the death investigation in 2016 with an accidental-death finding. Initial heart-attack accounts are superseded; subsequent contested theories are not treated as established facts.

No exact Forbes wealth-list profile was found. The interview is not offered as a Forbes profile. No verified personal LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, Twitter, YouTube, TikTok, Vimeo, Flickr or personal website emerged from English/Russian searches and source-link review. The Main Road Post LinkedIn profile is a clearly rejected namesake. A transcript mentions Twitter use but supplies no verified handle.

The company domain gazprom-media.com was identified from its official appointment announcement, but direct retrieval failed; no company link is proposed. Corporate accounts and interview videos are not substituted for personal social profiles.

No secondary nationality is established. California family homes and visits do not by themselves verify a secondary residence country, so none is proposed. Existing patronymic transliteration and verified birth/death fields remain unchanged.

Founding histories use differing predecessor dates; no exact founding year is stated in prose. Gazprom-Media resignation was announced in December 2014 with formal succession in early 2015; no conflicting exact end date is asserted.
The immutable source has South as a historical vessel relationship from 2008 toNovember 2015. Vessel data is identity context only; no current ownership is asserted.
